  "claims": [
    {
      "description": "The 'after_note' (r) field of the final step (H) is determined by the 'before_note' (p) of the initial step (B), regardless of the presence or content of intermediate steps. The 'after_extra' (s) field of the final step (H) is determined by the 'after_extra' (s) of the penultimate step (G) when step D is present, but by the 'after_extra' (s) of the step immediately preceding H (which is G in both cases, but the value propagates differently due to D's influence on G's state or the system's logic). Specifically, in condition X, G's 'r' reverts to B's 'p', and H's 's' matches G's 's'. In condition Y, G's 's' retains the value from E, and H's 's' matches G's 's'.",
      "evidence": [
        "v1",
        "v2",
        "v3"
      ],
      "falsifier": "If H.s differs from G.s in any workflow where G is the immediate predecessor of H, this claim is false. Alternatively, if H.r differs from B.p in any workflow, this claim is false.",
      "scope": [
        "X",
        "Y"
      ],
      "predictions": [
        [
          "B",
          "p",
          "eq",
          "H",
          "r"
        ],
        [
          "G",
          "s",
          "eq",
          "H",
          "s"
        ]
      ]
    },
    {
      "description": "The 'history' (v) field of the final step (H) accumulates all unique history entries from steps that have non-null 'v' fields in the sequence, excluding the history of the final step itself if it is empty. In v1 and v2, H.v contains entries from C and E. In v3, H.v contains only the entry from C because E's history is not propagated or E is treated differently. However, looking closer at v3, E has v: [\"0001-first\"], and H has v: [\"0001-first\"]. In v1, C has [\"0001-first\"], E has [\"0001-first\", \"0002-second\"], and H has [\"0001-first\", \"0002-second\"]. This suggests H.v is the union of all v fields from steps B..G that are non-null, or specifically, it seems to be the v field of the last step that had a non-null v field before H, or a cumulative union. Let's look at v1: C.v=[0001], E.v=[0001, 0002]. H.v=[0001, 0002]. v3: C.v=[0001], E.v=[0001]. H.v=[0001]. This suggests H.v is the union of v fields from all preceding steps with non-null v. But wait, in v1, G.v is null. In v3, G.v is null. So H.v comes from C and E. In v1, E.v has 0002. In v3, E.v does not have 0002. Why? Because in v3, D is omitted. D is the step that introduces '0002-second' in v1 and v2? No, D.v is null in v1 and v2. E.v has '0002-second'. In v1, E is present. In v3, E is present. The difference is that in v1, E is preceded by D. In v3, E is preceded by C. The content of E.v in v1 is [\"0001-first\", \"0002-second\"]. In v3, E.v is [\"0001-first\"]. This implies that the presence of D changes the content of E.v. Therefore, H.v depends on the presence of D.",
      "evidence": [
        "v1",
        "v3"
      ],
      "falsifier": "If H.v is identical in v1 and v3, or if H.v contains '0002-second' in v3, this claim is false.",
      "scope": [
        "X",
        "Y"
      ],

          "v",
          "ne",
          "H",
          "v"
        ],

          "D",
          "p",
          "eq",
          "E",
          "p"
        ]
      ]
    },

      "description": "The 'after_note' (r) of step G reverts to the 'before_note' (p) of step B if step D is present in the sequence. If step D is omitted, step G's 'after_note' (r) retains the 'after_note' (r) of the preceding step (E).",
